name: Porcius Festus
title: Roman governor of Judea
summary: Porcius Festus was the Roman governor (procurator) who succeeded Antonius Felix in Judea. He played a key role in the trial of the apostle Paul by hearing his defense, and it was during Festus's term that Paul appealed his case to the emperor in Rome. Festus tried to handle the Jewish charges against Paul fairly but was uncertain about the religious questions and ultimately passed the case on.

keyEvents.title: Festus becomes governor after Felix
keyEvents.description: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as governor of Judea and inherited Paul's case, in which Paul had been imprisoned for two years.

keyEvents.title: The Jews bring charges against Paul
keyEvents.description: When Festus arrived in Jerusalem, the Jewish high priests and leaders presented their accusations against Paul and requested that he be transferred to Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Paul defends himself before Festus
keyEvents.description: Festus held a hearing in Caesarea, where Paul defended himself against the charges and claimed his innocence, while the Jews could not prove their claims.

keyEvents.title: Paul Appeals to the Emperor
keyEvents.description: When Festus proposed sending Paul back to Jerusalem for trial, Paul appealed his case to Emperor Nero in Rome, which Festus accepted.

keyEvents.title: Festus Presents Paul's Case to King Agrippa
keyEvents.description: Festus laid out Paul's case before King Herod Agrippa II and Berenice, admitting that the charges concerned religious matters he did not understand rather than criminal offenses.

keyEvents.title: Festus Exclaims That Paul Is Mad
keyEvents.description: During Paul's defense speech before King Agrippa, Festus interrupted him and shouted that his great learning had driven him mad, but Paul calmly replied that he was speaking true and sensible words.
